criteria.evidence: Turn 0: the second revision dir is a 'stray fixture' proving the mirror scopes ~/snap/hello by what pc2's snapd holds, tied to §6's 'no second revision directory' check.

Turns 3-4: 'There's no ssh binary anywhere on this machine... exit 127 on every attempt'; verdict then grounded in ADR-020 measurements, flatpak_sync.py and the unit test (turn 1 initially asked the user to run commands, but the final investigation was from the repository).
Turn 2: 'not a pc-switcher bug, it's the runbook step itself' — an allow-only filter narrows nothing, so remote-ls still lists sopwith and the check correctly does not fire.
Diff §3: printf 'deny *\nallow org.freedesktop.*\n' > /home/testuser/uat.filter (pc2.filter also fixed and disclosed).
Turn 6: 'This one's a real bug, not a runbook issue — and I fixed the code this time'.

Replay chose to change behaviour: registry loaded at top of plan() before capture_source_items(), regression test added and shown to fail on old ordering; choice stated in turn 6 ('No runbook change needed... the code just didn't deliver it').
§4 now reads 'the collateral question "remove fortunes-min from pc2, so fortunes is removed as well"' — the on-screen hint, with reply naming key `y`/`remove`; 'go ahead' removed.
§4: 'the repository deletion `<s>` — apt's own second review round, asked once the first round's answers are in, still before snap_sync starts'.

§5 bullet 'snap_sync asks `Install snap packages` first, for `hello-world` alone... starts applied... needing only a confirm'; §4 places it after repo deletion and before hello's change (§4's '`<x>` left at install' wording is a bit confusing).

§5 bullet 'flatpak_sync asks `Install flatpak applications` for `io.github.fragglet.sdl_sopwith` alone... needing only a confirm'; §4 places it after hello's change and before the /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor question.
Turn 10: shape is undecidable from the layout; 'pick "one application" not because it's more correct, but to stay consistent with the rest of the script' (§4/§5/§6 assume a single finding).
§4: 'answered "one application" while still planning; then its review presents `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` first, answered `<y>`..., and `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor` second, answered `<x>`'.
Turn 12-13: 'I don't have live access to pc1/pc2'; explains _hold_snap_autorefresh is skipped in --dry-run so snapd's auto-refresh moved pc2's hello back to pc1's revision.
Turn 14 adds and describes the remedy: re-pin hello on pc2 with `sudo snap refresh --revision=<that second revision> hello` before every invocation, with a `snap changes` fallback check.
§4 new paragraph: 'Re-pin `hello` on pc2 before every invocation of either command above, dry run or real, first time or a repeat' with the ssh/snap refresh command.
Full unit suite 4354 passed, 1 pre-existing failure from missing rsync binary; reply states ruff/format and basedpyright clean on touched files; codespell run not observable in record.

judge.reason: Every criterion is addressed: the filter fix, collateral/second-round wording, missing hello-world and sdl_sopwith screens, review ordering, 'one application' justification and the re-pin instruction are all in the runbook diff, and the unreachable VMs were explicitly acknowledged with code-based reasoning. Doubt remains over §4's confusing '`<x>` left at install' phrasing for the two install rows, the unverified codespell run, and the replay's choice to fix check 3 in code (a defensible but unconfirmed reading of the runbook's intent).
